newsitem.title: USA: PSA criticizes Clinton FY'98 "de minimis" proposal.
newsitem.headline: PSA criticizes Clinton FY'98 "de minimis" proposal.

text.p: Bond dealers on Thursday criticized a part of President Clinton's proposed fiscal 1998 budget that would repeal the two percent "de minimis" rule on corporate holdings of tax-exempt bonds.

Micah Green, executive vice president of PSA The Bond Market Trade Association, said de minimis repeal would "raise the cost of financing new investment in public infrastructure and other job-creating assets."
The President's proposal, which is designed to raise revenues for financially stretched federal government, "is disguised as a tax increase on corporations," Green said.
"In reality, the tax would be borne by states and localities by increasing their cost of borrowing in the short-term andof leasing capital assets," green said in a four-page press statement.
Green said the proposal also would raise the cost of home mortgage financing provided to low- and middle-income families through state and local mortgage bond programs.
"We fully support a balanced federal budget, but we don't think it's fair to balance the budget on the backs of working families who are struggling to buy homes," Green said.
Green said his group is pleased that the President delayed the proposed effective date of the plan to whenever it is voted on by a congressional committee.
A similar Clinton proposal in 1995 to repeal de minimis had an immediate effective date, which "shut down" activity on some bonds, Green said.
